newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama has no warrants for Haitian coup leaders.
newsitem.headline: Panama has no warrants for Haitian coup leaders.

text.p: Panama has not yet received an official Haitian request to arrest exiled leaders of a 1991 military coup that overthrew former Haiti President Jean- Bertrand Aristide, a government spokesman said on Sunday.

"We have received information on the telephone about the arrest warrants, but nothing official," Foreign Ministry spokesman Erich Rodriguez Auerbach told the daily newspaper El Panama America in its Sunday edition.

Five days ago, the Haitian government issued new arrest warrants for former army chief of staff Phillipe Biamby and Yannick Cedras, the wife of coup leader Gen. Raoul Cedras, who are living in exile in a wealthy neighbourhood in Panama City.

Haiti's Foreign Affairs Minister Fritz Longchamps said his advisers were deliberating over whether the government would file an extradition request to return Mrs. Cedras and Biamby to Haitian courts to answer charges against them.
"They are wanted for various acts of corruption, for stealing property of the state," said Justice Minister Max Antoine.

A recently released CIA document said Biamby and his associates coordinated the murder of Justice Minister Guy Malary with members of the Revolutionary Front for Haitian Advancement and Progress (FRAPH).
Biamby left Haiti for Panama with Cedras on a U.S. military plane when the military regime collapsed with the arrival of U.S. troops to restore Aristide in 1994.
